sanskrit: tasminn ākruśyati droṇe maharṣitanaye tadā nīcātmanā nṛśaṃsena kṣudreṇa gurughātinā
english: When that son of the great sage, Droṇa, was thus reviled—reviled by a base-souled, cruel, and contemptible slayer of his own teacher—

sanskrit: yasya prasādāt karmāṇi kurvanti puruṣarṣabhāḥ amānuṣāṇi saṃgrāme devair asukarāṇi ca
english: by whose grace those bulls among men perform feats in battle that are more than human, deeds hard even for the gods to accomplish—

sanskrit: tasminn ākruśyati droṇe samakṣaṃ pāpakarmiṇaḥ nāmarṣaṃ tatra kurvanti dhik kṣatraṃ dhig amarṣitam
english: when Droṇa was thus reviled before their very eyes by that doer of evil deeds, they showed no resentment. A curse upon the kṣatriya order, and a curse upon their want of indignation!

sanskrit: pārthāḥ sarve ca rājānaḥ pṛthivyāṃ ye dhanurdharāḥ śrutvā kim āhuḥ pāñcālyaṃ tan mamācakṣva saṃjaya
english: What did all the sons of Pṛthā and the kings of the earth who bear the bow say when they heard the Pāñcāla prince? Tell me that, Saṃjaya.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca śrutvā drupadaputrasya tā vācaḥ krūrakarmaṇaḥ tūṣṇīṃ babhūvū rājānaḥ sarva eva viśāṃ pate
english: Saṃjaya said: Having heard those words of Drupada's son, that doer of cruel deeds, all the kings fell silent, O lord of peoples.

sanskrit: arjunas tu kaṭākṣeṇa jihmaṃ prekṣya ca pārṣatam sabāṣpam abhiniḥśvasya dhig dhig dhig iti cābravīt
english: But Arjuna, eyeing the son of Pṛṣata askance with a sidelong glance, sighed with tears in his eyes and said, 'Shame, shame, shame!'

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhiraś ca bhīmaś ca yamau kṛṣṇas tathāpare āsan suvrīḍitā rājan sātyakir idam abravīt
english: Yudhiṣṭhira and Bhīma, the twins, Kṛṣṇa, and the others were sorely abashed, O king, and Sātyaki spoke these words:

sanskrit: nehāsti puruṣaḥ kaś cid ya imaṃ pāpapūruṣam bhāṣamāṇam akalyāṇaṃ śīghraṃ hanyān narādhamam
english: 'Is there here no man who would swiftly strike down this wicked wretch, this vilest of men, as he utters words so unholy?

sanskrit: kathaṃ ca śatadhā jihvā na te mūrdhā ca dīryate gurum ākrośataḥ kṣudra na cādharmeṇa pātyase
english: How is it, base one, that your tongue does not split into a hundred pieces and your head burst asunder, when you revile your teacher, and how is it that you are not cast down by your own unrighteousness?

sanskrit: yāpyas tvam asi pārthaiś ca sarvaiś cāndhakavṛṣṇibhiḥ yat karma kaluṣaṃ kṛtvā ślāghase janasaṃsadi
english: You are to be reproached by the sons of Pṛthā and by all the Andhakas and Vṛṣṇis, for having done so foul a deed you yet boast of it in the assembly of men.

sanskrit: akāryaṃ tādṛśaṃ kṛtvā punar eva guruṃ kṣipan vadhyas tvaṃ na tvayārtho 'sti muhūrtam api jīvatā
english: Having committed such an undoable deed and now reviling your teacher besides, you deserve death; there is no profit in your living even for a single moment.

sanskrit: kas tv etad vyavased āryas tvad anyaḥ puruṣādhamaḥ nigṛhya keśeṣu vadhaṃ guror dharmātmanaḥ sataḥ
english: What noble man other than you, vilest of men, would have resolved upon this—to seize by the hair and slay a teacher, righteous and good?

sanskrit: saptāvare tathā pūrve bāndhavās te nipātitāḥ yaśasā ca parityaktās tvāṃ prāpya kulapāṃsanam
english: Seven generations of your kinsmen, those before and those to come, have been cast down and forsaken by their renown, having gotten you, the defiler of your line.

sanskrit: uktavāṃś cāpi yat pārthaṃ bhīṣmaṃ prati nararṣabham tathānto vihitas tena svayam eva mahātmanā
english: And as for what you said to Pārtha concerning Bhīṣma, that bull among men—the end of that great-souled one was ordained by his very own self.

sanskrit: tasyāpi tava sodaryo nihantā pāpakṛttamaḥ nānyaḥ pāñcālaputrebhyo vidyate bhuvi pāpakṛt
english: And of him too the slayer was your own brother, that doer of the worst of deeds; no greater doer of evil than the sons of Pāñcāla is to be found upon the earth.

sanskrit: sa cāpi sṛṣṭaḥ pitrā te bhīṣmasyāntakaraḥ kila śikhaṇḍī rakṣitas tena sa ca mṛtyur mahātmanaḥ
english: And he too, Śikhaṇḍin, was begotten by your father to be the bringer of Bhīṣma's end; he was guarded by Arjuna, and he became the death of that great-souled one.

sanskrit: pāñcālāś calitā dharmāt kṣudrā mitragurudruhaḥ tvāṃ prāpya sahasodaryaṃ dhikkṛtaṃ sarvasādhubhiḥ
english: The Pāñcālas have fallen from righteousness, base traitors to friend and teacher, having gotten you together with your brother, condemned by all good men.

sanskrit: punaś ced īdṛśīṃ vācaṃ matsamīpe vadiṣyasi śiras te pātayiṣyāmi gadayā vajrakalpayā
english: If once again you utter such words in my presence, I shall strike off your head with my mace, mighty as the thunderbolt.'

sanskrit: sātvatenaivam ākṣiptaḥ pārṣataḥ paruṣākṣaram saṃrabdhaḥ sātyakiṃ prāha saṃkruddhaḥ prahasann iva
english: Thus assailed by the Sātvata with harsh syllables, the son of Pṛṣata, enraged, spoke to Sātyaki in wrath, yet as though laughing:

sanskrit: śrūyate śrūyate ceti kṣamyate ceti mādhava na cānārya śubhaṃ sādhuṃ puruṣaṃ kṣeptum arhasi
english: 'It is heard, it is heard—and it is borne, it is borne, O Mādhava. But you, ignoble one, ought not to revile a good and worthy man.

sanskrit: kṣamā praśasyate loke na tu pāpo 'rhati kṣamām kṣamāvantaṃ hi pāpātmā jito 'yam iti manyate
english: Forbearance is praised in the world, but the wicked man does not deserve forbearance; for the evil-souled one thinks of the forbearing man, "This one is beaten."

sanskrit: sa tvaṃ kṣudrasamācāro nīcātmā pāpaniścayaḥ ā keśāgrān nakhāgrāc ca vaktavyo vaktum icchasi
english: You, of mean conduct, base-souled, and fixed upon evil, deserve to be reproached from the tips of your hair to the tips of your nails—yet you wish to speak.

sanskrit: yaḥ sa bhūriśravāś chinne bhuje prāyagatas tvayā vāryamāṇena nihatas tataḥ pāpataraṃ nu kim
english: That Bhūriśravas, his arm severed and seated in the vow of fasting to death, was slain by you though you were being restrained—what is more wicked than that?

sanskrit: vyūhamāno mayā droṇo divyenāstreṇa saṃyuge visṛṣṭaśastro nihataḥ kiṃ tatra krūra duṣkṛtam
english: As I shielded Droṇa with a celestial weapon in the fray, he was slain when he had laid down his arms—what cruel ill deed is there in that, you savage?

sanskrit: ayudhyamānaṃ yas tv ājau tathā prāyagataṃ munim chinnabāhuṃ parair hanyāt sātyake sa kathaṃ bhavet
english: But he who would slay in battle, with another's help, a sage not fighting, seated in the vow of death, his arm already severed—what manner of man is he, O Sātyaki?

sanskrit: nihatya tvāṃ yadā bhūmau sa vikrāmati vīryavān kiṃ tadā na nihaṃsy enaṃ bhūtvā puruṣasattamaḥ
english: When that valiant one, having struck you to the ground, was striding upon you, why did you not then slay him, you who would be the best of men?

sanskrit: tvayā punar anāryeṇa pūrvaṃ pārthena nirjitaḥ yadā tadā hataḥ śūraḥ saumadattiḥ pratāpavān
english: But the heroic son of Somadatta, glorious in might, was first vanquished by Pārtha and then slain by you, ignoble one.

sanskrit: yatra yatra tu pāṇḍūnāṃ droṇo drāvayate camūm kirañ śarasahasrāṇi tatra tatra prayāmy aham
english: Wherever Droṇa, scattering thousands of arrows, put the host of the Pāṇḍavas to flight, thither and thither did I go.

sanskrit: sa tvam evaṃvidhaṃ kṛtvā karma cāṇḍālavat svayam vaktum icchasi vaktavyaḥ kasmān māṃ paruṣāṇy atha
english: Having yourself done such a deed, like an outcaste, why then do you, who deserve reproach, wish to speak harsh words to me?

sanskrit: kartā tvaṃ karmaṇograsya nāhaṃ vṛṣṇikulādhama pāpānāṃ ca tvam āvāsaḥ karmaṇāṃ mā punar vada
english: You are the doer of that ghastly deed, not I, O basest of the Vṛṣṇi line; you are the dwelling-place of wicked deeds—speak no more.

sanskrit: joṣam āssva na māṃ bhūyo vaktum arhasy ataḥ param adharottaram etad dhi yan mā tvaṃ vaktum icchasi
english: Hold your peace; you ought not to address me further from here on, for this that you wish to say to me is utter nonsense, the lowest set above the highest.

sanskrit: atha vakṣyasi māṃ maurkhyād bhūyaḥ paruṣam īdṛśam gamayiṣyāmi bāṇais tvāṃ yudhi vaivasvatakṣayam
english: And if out of folly you address such harsh words to me again, I shall send you with my arrows in battle to the abode of Vaivasvata.

sanskrit: na caiva mūrkha dharmeṇa kevalenaiva śakyate teṣām api hy adharmeṇa ceṣṭitaṃ śṛṇu yādṛśam
english: And not by righteousness alone, you fool, can it be done; hear what manner of unrighteous deeds were wrought even by these.

sanskrit: vañcitaḥ pāṇḍavaḥ pūrvam adharmeṇa yudhiṣṭhiraḥ draupadī ca parikliṣṭā tathādharmeṇa sātyake
english: The Pāṇḍava Yudhiṣṭhira was first deceived through unrighteousness, and Draupadī too was tormented likewise through unrighteousness, O Sātyaki.

sanskrit: pravrājitā vanaṃ sarve pāṇḍavāḥ saha kṛṣṇayā sarvasvam apakṛṣṭaṃ ca tathādharmeṇa bāliśa
english: All the Pāṇḍavas were sent into exile in the forest together with Kṛṣṇā, and all their possessions were stripped away likewise through unrighteousness, you simpleton.

sanskrit: adharmeṇāpakṛṣṭaś ca madrarājaḥ parair itaḥ ito 'py adharmeṇa hato bhīṣmaḥ kurupitāmahaḥ bhūriśravā hy adharmeṇa tvayā dharmavidā hataḥ
english: And the king of the Madras was drawn off from this side by his foes through unrighteousness; and from this side too Bhīṣma, the grandsire of the Kurus, was slain through unrighteousness; and Bhūriśravas was slain through unrighteousness by you, knower of righteousness though you be.

sanskrit: evaṃ parair ācaritaṃ pāṇḍaveyaiś ca saṃyuge rakṣamāṇair jayaṃ vīrair dharmajñair api sātvata
english: Thus was it practiced in battle by your foes and by the Pāṇḍavas alike—by heroes who, though knowers of righteousness, were guarding their victory, O Sātvata.

sanskrit: durjñeyaḥ paramo dharmas tathādharmaḥ sudurvidaḥ yudhyasva kauravaiḥ sārdhaṃ mā gāḥ pitṛniveśanam
english: The highest righteousness is hard to know, and so too unrighteousness is most difficult to discern. Fight with the Kauravas; go not to the dwelling of your fathers.'

sanskrit: evamādīni vākyāni krūrāṇi paruṣāṇi ca śrāvitaḥ sātyakiḥ śrīmān ākampita ivābhavat
english: Made to hear these and other words, cruel and harsh, the illustrious Sātyaki became as though shaken.

sanskrit: tac chrutvā krodhatāmrākṣaḥ sātyakis tv ādade gadām viniḥśvasya yathā sarpaḥ praṇidhāya rathe dhanuḥ
english: Hearing this, Sātyaki, his eyes copper-red with wrath, took up his mace, hissing like a serpent, having set down his bow upon the chariot.

sanskrit: tato 'bhipatya pāñcālyaṃ saṃrambheṇedam abravīt na tvāṃ vakṣyāmi paruṣaṃ haniṣye tvāṃ vadhakṣamam
english: Then rushing upon the Pāñcāla, he said this in his fury: 'I will not speak harsh words to you; I will slay you, who deserve death.'

sanskrit: tam āpatantaṃ sahasā mahābalam amarṣaṇam pāñcālyāyābhisaṃkruddham antakāyāntakopamam
english: As he fell suddenly upon the Pāñcāla, mighty, impatient of insult, and wrathful, like Death itself against another Death—

sanskrit: codito vāsudevena bhīmaseno mahābalaḥ avaplutya rathāt tūrṇaṃ bāhubhyāṃ samavārayat
english: urged on by Vāsudeva, the mighty Bhīmasena leapt swiftly from his chariot and held him back with both his arms.

sanskrit: dravamāṇaṃ tathā kruddhaṃ sātyakiṃ pāṇḍavo balī praskandamānam ādāya jagāma balinaṃ balāt
english: The strong Pāṇḍava, seizing the wrathful Sātyaki as he rushed and struggled forward, dragged the powerful one back by force.

sanskrit: sthitvā viṣṭabhya caraṇau bhīmena śinipuṃgavaḥ nigṛhītaḥ pade ṣaṣṭhe balena balināṃ varaḥ
english: Standing firm and planting his feet, Bhīma held back that bull of Śini's line, the foremost of the strong, by main strength at the sixth step.

sanskrit: avaruhya rathāt taṃ tu hriyamāṇaṃ balīyasā uvāca ślakṣṇayā vācā sahadevo viśāṃ pate
english: And Sahadeva, descending from his chariot, spoke to him in gentle words as he was being dragged back by the stronger one, O lord of peoples:

sanskrit: asmākaṃ puruṣavyāghra mitram anyan na vidyate param andhakavṛṣṇibhyaḥ pāñcālebhyaś ca mādhava
english: 'O tiger among men, no other friend higher than the Andhakas and Vṛṣṇis and the Pāñcālas is known to us, O Mādhava.

sanskrit: tathaivāndhakavṛṣṇīnāṃ tava caiva viśeṣataḥ kṛṣṇasya ca tathāsmatto mitram anyan na vidyate
english: And so too for the Andhakas and Vṛṣṇis, and for you in particular, and for Kṛṣṇa, no other friend than ourselves is known.

sanskrit: pāñcālānāṃ ca vārṣṇeya samudrāntāṃ vicinvatām nānyad asti paraṃ mitraṃ yathā pāṇḍavavṛṣṇayaḥ
english: And for the Pāñcālas too, O scion of Vṛṣṇi, were they to search to the very shores of the ocean, there is no other friend so great as the Pāṇḍavas and Vṛṣṇis are to one another.

sanskrit: sa bhavān īdṛśaṃ mitraṃ manyate ca yathā bhavān bhavantaś ca yathāsmākaṃ bhavatāṃ ca tathā vayam
english: You regard such a friend even as he regards you; and as you are to us, so are we to you.

sanskrit: sa evaṃ sarvadharmajño mitradharmam anusmaran niyaccha manyuṃ pāñcālyāt praśāmya śinipuṃgava
english: Therefore, you who know all righteousness, remembering the duty owed to a friend, restrain your wrath against the Pāñcāla and be appeased, O bull of Śini's line.

sanskrit: pārṣatasya kṣama tvaṃ vai kṣamatāṃ tava pārṣataḥ vayaṃ kṣamayitāraś ca kim anyatra śamād bhavet
english: Forgive the son of Pṛṣata, and let the son of Pṛṣata forgive you; we are here to make peace between you—what is there to gain apart from calm?'

sanskrit: praśāmyamāne śaineye sahadevena māriṣa pāñcālarājasya sutaḥ prahasann idam abravīt
english: As the grandson of Śini was being pacified by Sahadeva, O honored one, the son of the Pāñcāla king said this, laughing:

sanskrit: muñca muñca śineḥ pautraṃ bhīma yuddhamadānvitam āsādayatu mām eṣa dharādharam ivānilaḥ
english: 'Release, release the grandson of Śini, Bhīma, possessed as he is by the frenzy of battle; let him come at me as the wind comes against a mountain.

sanskrit: yāvad asya śitair bāṇaiḥ saṃrambhaṃ vinayāmy aham yuddhaśraddhāṃ ca kaunteya jīvitasya ca saṃyuge
english: that with my sharp arrows I may quell his fury, his appetite for battle, and his very hold on life in the fray, O son of Kuntī.

sanskrit: kiṃ nu śakyaṃ mayā kartuṃ kāryaṃ yad idam udyatam sumahat pāṇḍuputrāṇām āyānty ete hi kauravāḥ
english: But what indeed can I do? A great task is upon the sons of Pāṇḍu, for here the Kauravas are advancing.

sanskrit: atha vā phalgunaḥ sarvān vārayiṣyati saṃyuge aham apy asya mūrdhānaṃ pātayiṣyāmi sāyakaiḥ
english: Or else Phalguna will hold them all back in battle; and I too shall strike off this man's head with my arrows.

sanskrit: manyate chinnabāhuṃ māṃ bhūriśravasam āhave utsṛjainam ahaṃ vainam eṣa māṃ vā haniṣyati
english: He thinks me a Bhūriśravas with severed arm in the battle. Let him go—either I shall slay him, or he shall slay me.'

sanskrit: śṛṇvan pāñcālavākyāni sātyakiḥ sarpavac chvasan bhīmabāhvantare sakto visphuraty aniśaṃ balī
english: Hearing the words of the Pāñcāla, Sātyaki, hissing like a serpent, the mighty one held fast in the clasp of Bhīma's arms, writhed without ceasing.

sanskrit: tvarayā vāsudevaś ca dharmarājaś ca māriṣa yatnena mahatā vīrau vārayām āsatus tataḥ
english: Then in haste Vāsudeva and the Dharma King, O honored one, with great effort held back those two heroes.

sanskrit: nivārya parameṣvāsau krodhasaṃraktalocanau yuyutsavaḥ parān saṃkhye pratīyuḥ kṣatriyarṣabhāḥ
english: Having restrained those two great archers, their eyes red with wrath, those bulls among kṣatriyas, eager for combat, advanced against their foes in battle.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tataḥ sa kadanaṃ cakre ripūṇāṃ droṇanandanaḥ yugānte sarvabhūtānāṃ kālasṛṣṭa ivāntakaḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: Then the son of Droṇa wrought havoc among his foes, like Death created by Time at the end of an age to destroy all beings.

sanskrit: dhvajadrumaṃ śastraśṛṅgaṃ hatanāgamahāśilam aśvakiṃpuruṣākīrṇaṃ śarāsanalatāvṛtam
english: With banners for its trees and weapons for its peaks, slain elephants for its great boulders, strewn with horses and kiṃpuruṣas, and overgrown with bows for creepers—

sanskrit: śūlakravyādasaṃghuṣṭaṃ bhūtayakṣagaṇākulam nihatya śātravān bhallaiḥ so 'cinod dehaparvatam
english: resounding with pikes and flesh-eating beasts, thronged with hosts of spirits and yakṣas—having slain his enemies with his broad-headed arrows, he heaped up a mountain of corpses.

sanskrit: tato vegena mahatā vinadya sa nararṣabhaḥ pratijñāṃ śrāvayām āsa punar eva tavātmajam
english: Then with great vehemence that bull among men roared aloud and proclaimed his vow once more to your son:

sanskrit: yasmād yudhyantam ācāryaṃ dharmakañcukam āsthitaḥ muñca śastram iti prāha kuntīputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: 'Because, while my teacher was fighting, Kuntī's son Yudhiṣṭhira, donning righteousness as a coat of mail, said to him, "Lay down your weapon"—

sanskrit: tasmāt saṃpaśyatas tasya drāvayiṣyāmi vāhinīm vidrāvya satyaṃ hantāsmi pāpaṃ pāñcālyam eva tu
english: therefore, before his very eyes, I shall rout his host; and having routed it, in truth I shall slay that wicked Pāñcāla.

sanskrit: sarvān etān haniṣyāmi yadi yotsyanti māṃ raṇe satyaṃ te pratijānāmi parāvartaya vāhinīm
english: I shall slay all of these if they fight me in battle—this I truly vow to you. Turn back your host!'

sanskrit: tac chrutvā tava putras tu vāhinīṃ paryavartayat siṃhanādena mahatā vyapohya sumahad bhayam
english: Hearing this, your son turned the host about, dispelling its great fear with a mighty lion's roar.

sanskrit: tataḥ samāgamo rājan kurupāṇḍavasenayoḥ punar evābhavat tīvraḥ pūrṇasāgarayor iva
english: Then, O king, the clash of the Kuru and Pāṇḍava armies arose once more, fierce as that of two full oceans meeting.

sanskrit: saṃrabdhā hi sthirībhūtā droṇaputreṇa kauravāḥ udagrāḥ pāṇḍupāñcālā droṇasya nidhanena ca
english: For the Kauravas, enraged, were made steadfast by the son of Droṇa, while the Pāṇḍavas and Pāñcālas were exultant at the slaying of Droṇa.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ paramahṛṣṭānāṃ jayam ātmani paśyatām saṃrabdhānāṃ mahāvegaḥ prādurāsīd raṇājire
english: A mighty onrush arose upon the field of battle from those exceedingly joyful warriors, who, enraged, saw victory already within their grasp.

sanskrit: yathā śiloccaye śailaḥ sāgare sāgaro yathā pratihanyeta rājendra tathāsan kurupāṇḍavāḥ
english: As a mountain might dash against a mountain, or an ocean against an ocean, O lord of kings, so were the Kurus and the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: tataḥ śaṅkhasahasrāṇi bherīṇām ayutāni ca avādayanta saṃhṛṣṭāḥ kurupāṇḍavasainikāḥ
english: Then the soldiers of the Kurus and Pāṇḍavas, full of joy, sounded thousands of conches and tens of thousands of kettledrums.

sanskrit: tato nirmathyamānasya sāgarasyeva nisvanaḥ abhavat tasya sainyasya sumahān adbhutopamaḥ
english: Then there arose from that army a tumult, exceedingly great and wondrous, like the roar of an ocean being churned.

sanskrit: prāduścakre tato drauṇir astraṃ nārāyaṇaṃ tadā abhisaṃdhāya pāṇḍūnāṃ pāñcālānāṃ ca vāhinīm
english: Then the son of Droṇa brought forth the Nārāyaṇa weapon, aiming it at the host of the Pāṇḍavas and Pāñcālas.

sanskrit: prādurāsaṃs tato bāṇā dīptāgrāḥ khe sahasraśaḥ pāṇḍavān bhakṣayiṣyanto dīptāsyā iva pannagāḥ
english: Then there appeared in the sky arrows by the thousand, their points ablaze, eager to devour the Pāṇḍavas like serpents with flaming jaws.

sanskrit: te diśaḥ khaṃ ca sainyaṃ ca samāvṛṇvan mahāhave muhūrtād bhāskarasyeva rājaṃl lokaṃ gabhastayaḥ
english: In that great battle they shrouded the quarters, the sky, and the army in a moment, O king, as the rays of the sun cover the world.

sanskrit: tathāpare dyotamānā jyotīṃṣīvāmbare 'male prādurāsan mahīpāla kārṣṇāyasamayā guḍāḥ
english: And others appeared, blazing like stars in a clear sky, O guardian of the earth—balls wrought of black iron.

sanskrit: caturdiśaṃ vicitrāś ca śataghnyo 'tha hutāśadāḥ cakrāṇi ca kṣurāntāni maṇḍalānīva bhāsvataḥ
english: And on every side appeared wondrous śataghnīs spewing fire, and razor-edged discuses, like the radiant orbs of the sun.
